name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Sunday 31 May 1987

clue.text: Do rich characters produce a tropical flower

indicators.note: the characters of the phrase are made to produce something new by being rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether wealthy people grow exotic blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Many orchids grow wild in the tropics, so a tropical flower is a fair description by example.

clue.text: Of musical drama, some give no-hoper a ticket

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying across the words

blocks.note: the letters run across no-hoper, a and ticket

explanation.surface: Someone at the opera hands a spare ticket to a hopeless case.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is drama set to music, so the adjective describing it means relating to musical drama.

clue.text: The elm reshaped to make some protective wear

indicators.note: a thing reshaped has its parts set in a new form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Wood from an elm tree is carved into a piece of armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet is a hard covering worn on the head for safety, one item of protective gear.

clue.text: The maiden, no hardhead, could develop madness

indicators.note: saying the maiden has none of it means that letter is taken away
what remains could develop into something else by being reordered

blocks.note: the head, or first letter, of hard

explanation.surface: A young woman who is not stubborn might nonetheless lose her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardhead' reads as a stubborn person, but it is the head of the word hard; remove that H from THE MAIDEN and rearrange the rest into DEMENTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dementia is a severe decline of the mind, loosely used for insanity.

clue.text: Wager on a letter from Athens

explanation.surface: Someone places a bet on a letter posted from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second character of the Greek alphabet, the one used in Athens.

clue.text: 99 real constituents make this cake

indicators.note: the constituents are used as raw parts to make something, so they are reassembled in another order

blocks.note: 99 in Roman numerals, one before a hundred

explanation.surface: A recipe that lists ninety-nine genuine ingredients for a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: IC is an old-style Roman numeral for 99, one subtracted from C.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream, a type of small cake.

clue.text: A redolence rising?

blocks.note: redolence is a fragrance or scent

explanation.surface: A smell drifting upward, as from a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the whole reads as a smell wafting up, while the last word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is the act of going up, which is what a rising is.

clue.text: Healthy use of the muscles is a duty Her Majesty is involved in

indicators.note: the monarch being involved in something places her inside it

blocks.note: excise is a tax or duty on goods
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's monogram

explanation.surface: The Queen takes part in physical training as a royal obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher; excise is the tax charged on goods such as alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise is physical activity working the body to keep fit, matching the healthy use described.

clue.text: Symbol derived from Member of British Empire and 2's tree

indicators.note: something derived from material is formed out of it, here by reordering the letters

blocks.note: MBE is the British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
the tree named in the clue for 2 down

explanation.surface: A badge designed from an imperial honour and a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue for 2 down is 'The elm reshaped...', so its tree is the elm.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a badge or device that stands for something, which is a symbol.

clue.text: Gives out, and in retrospect can be made to set a title

indicators.note: retrospect looks back, so the phrase is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: Someone issues honours and later regrets giving a title.
explanation.walkthrough: SET A NAME read backwards gives EMANATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, so emanates means gives out.

clue.text: -. because sea-bird is behind, nautically

explanation.surface: A sea-bird trails behind a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The '-.' at the start is debris from the scanned page and plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the sailor's term for at or towards the back of a vessel.

clue.text: Rashness, yet returns with inner merit

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
the other word goes on the inside, held within the turned word

explanation.surface: Recklessness that nevertheless comes back with hidden worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yet' reads as a conjunction in the surface, but it is just the word to turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is reckless boldness or audacity, the same quality as rashness.

clue.text: Later I am making some fabric

indicators.note: the letters are put to work making something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at a loom promising to weave cloth later.
explanation.definitionFit: Material is cloth or textile, so some material is an amount of fabric.

clue.text: Discoloured with age, shout out to be in debt for 500

blocks.note: to shout out is to yell
to owe is to be in debt

explanation.surface: An old document, faded with age, records a debt of 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper or paint that has yellowed has taken on a yellowish tinge through ageing.

clue.text: Agreement to make a kind of bridge?

blocks.note: first meaning: a binding legal agreement
second meaning: the commonest form of the card game bridge

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites you to think of a bridge over a river, but the bridge is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a formal deal between parties and is also the name of the standard form of the bidding card game.

clue.text: West Australian lout might become a proscribed person

indicators.note: the letters might become something else once they are rearranged

blocks.note: WA is the abbreviation for Western Australia

explanation.surface: A yob from Perth could end up banished by the law.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw was a person formally put outside the protection of the law, which is what proscribed means.

clue.text: Shake caused by some long-felt remorse

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying across two words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of long-felt and the start of remorse

explanation.surface: A guilty conscience makes someone tremble.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a trembling or quivering movement, a shake used as a noun.

clue.text: Is able to take five as essential part of artist's equipment

blocks.note: V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A painter who can take a five-minute break, as a key tool of the trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take five' reads as the idiom for a short break, but five is just the numeral V.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters work on stretched cloth, so the cloth surface is a basic part of their kit.

clue.text: Title in the Spanish for a hard, bright finish

indicators.note: one word goes in the other, placed inside it

blocks.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish title given to a glossy coating.
explanation.walkthrough: E(NAME)L: the title sits between the letters of the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glassy coating fused or painted on a surface to give a tough glossy finish.

clue.text: Holy man gives a lot of paper to the Queen for decoration

blocks.note: a ream is a large quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A saint hands the monarch a pile of paper for the festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long ribbon of paper hung up as festive ornament.

clue.text: Food for many to consume

blocks.note: M, the Roman thousand, stands for a large number
to consume food is to eat

explanation.surface: Enough to feed a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat once meant any solid food, as in 'meat and drink', and still means edible flesh.

clue.text: Can be seen if I get six to split new constituents

indicators.note: to split something is to break it open and get between its parts

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about six people breaking up a new party.
explanation.walkthrough: I, then NEW broken open by VI: I + N(VI)EW.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in view is visible, so the phrase stands for able to be seen.

clue.text: Wide view of father and mother taking in Nora

indicators.note: the parents taking someone in hold that person between them

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A family photo taken wide to fit the parents and Nora.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is an unbroken view over a wide area.

clue.text: Whipped fiercely in the French out-house

blocks.note: la is the French for the

explanation.surface: A punishment carried out in a French barn.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash is to strike hard with a whip, so lashed is whipped hard.
